verdicts.why: Confirmed on screen06.png (sentence 5). Line 2 of the Chinese translation ends with a lone Latin 'Z' ('…也就是人们所说的Z') and line 3 is only '世代。', so the term Z世代 is split across lines. The cause is in zh_html() in /home/user/university-entrance-examination/中考/tools/make_video.py: it wraps the last two Han characters plus the closing punctuation in a <nobr> so the last line always has at least two characters. That binds '世代。' together but not the Latin 'Z' in front of it. The browser then keeps 'Z' on line 2 and moves only the bound '世代。' down. Line 2 ends at about x=1070, against about 1175 for line 1, so there was room for more on that line. The text itself matches the reference; the defect is the line break. The suggested fix ('…所说的' / 'Z世代。') is correct.

The measurements in the report are accurate. On screen10.png (18 entries) the ink height of the Chinese meanings is about 21 px, against about 25 px on screen04.png (13 entries) and about 37 px on the 3–4-entry screens. About 220 px of panel width on the right is empty. But this is the intended auto-fit, not a defect. FIT shrinks the panel font (--vs) from 40 px until the list fits, and make_video.py enforces a readability floor of MIN_VS = 22: any sentence that would need a smaller size stops the build and must be split. Screen 10 comes out at about 22–23 px, so it meets the project's own minimum. The panel runs out of height, not width: the 18 entries fill it from about y=205 to y=945. Using the empty width would need a different layout, so that space is not wasted. Nothing is cut off or overlapping, and all 18 entries match reference sentence [9]. The reviewer also says nothing is wrong.
